A1.justification: Both readable, complete 20-page PDFs describe the same Plan and Budget work and contain Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the first-page code link and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MATH-500, NaturalInstructions, and TravelPlanner in Section 5 and Tables 3–5, plus difficulty-based analyses in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, numerical results, and Appendix F analyses. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The planning and local-budgeting procedure, decay schedulers, and prompt templates in Section 4 and Appendix G are identical.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same mathematical reasoning, instruction-following, and tool-free itinerary-planning tasks using MATH-500, NaturalInstructions, and TravelPlanner.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same Vanilla and Global Budget comparators, with and without planning, and the same local-budget variants. The standalone planner evaluation is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E retain identical samples, splits, reasoning models, planner, metrics, scheduler parameters, and the 8192-token cutoff.

E4.justification: The planning and scheduling comparisons in Tables 3–5 and the TravelPlanner difficulty and token-use analyses in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. No ablations or robustness analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report averages and standard deviations over five runs for all models and baselines in Section 5.1. Statistical reporting practices and uncertainty information are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 3–6, plotted results in Figures 3–4, and reported findings are identical. No scores, token counts, E3 values, or rankings change.

T1.justification: The E3 definition, BBAM assumptions and allocation equations, and uncertainty-decomposition, optimality, and unimodality derivations in Appendices A–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about training-free reasoning efficiency, headline gains, and narrowing the gap between smaller and larger models.

C2.justification: The uncertainty-based explanations and scheduler interpretations are identical. The extra planner-call limitation in the conclusion and inherited base-model limitations in Appendix D are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous 4open.science repository link with the named GitHub repository junhongmit/P-and-B, changing the documented code-access destination. Implementation details, compute disclosures, and prompts are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish changes to repository contents or availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations, all 37 reference entries, and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the abstract’s code-location text and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp change. The scientific prose, terminology, headings, and document organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–6 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Rendered pages 2–20 are identical, and the first-page text replacements preserve the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the complete scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations, and appendices. Updating an existing code link and the version stamp documents no scientific correction or additional reproducibility material, so the PDFs establish no meaningful overall quality difference.
